title: Customer status signal board - Inference rollout
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, lane-based signal board to use during weekly CS standups and QBR prep for inference rollouts. Intended for: CSMs, Solutions Eng, Delivery PMs. Goal is to keep the conversation focused on which customers need immediate action (red), which require watchful coordination (yellow), and which are on-track (green).

How to use:
- Maintain one row per customer / deployment.
- Update status lanes weekly before the CS standup.
- Add explicit owner and next action (owner + due date).
- Use the blockers section to capture cross-team escalations and required engineering work.

Legend (lane signals):
- GREEN: On schedule, milestones met, no unresolved infra/quality blockers. Renewal sentiment: neutral->positive.
- YELLOW: Minor risks (eg. perf variance, quota bumps, infra config). Active mitigation in flight. Renewal at-risk if not resolved within 2 sprints.
- RED: Critical blocker preventing go-live or causing severe production regressions (SLA misses, data exfil concerns, performance regression >30%, or security hold). Immediate escalation required.

Weekly snapshot template (copy into a sheet or the drive doc before the meeting):
- Customer: <short name>
- Product / Environment: hosted | dedicated | private (VPC/onprem)
- Current lane: GREEN | YELLOW | RED
- Milestone phase: planning / staging / canary / production
- Owner (CS): <name>
- Owner (SE/Delivery): <name>
- Primary blocker (if any): <short description>
- Next action & owner & date: <e.g., SE to repro perf with 2k samples by 2025-02-10>
- Renewal signal: on_track | watch | at_risk | early_renewal
- Notes (free-form): <links to PRs, runbooks, logs>

Example entry (realistic mock):
- Customer: Athena HealthTech
- Product / Environment: dedicated (EU-west)
- Current lane: YELLOW
- Milestone phase: canary
- Owner (CS): Aisha Patel
- Owner (SE/Delivery): Miguel Torres
- Primary blocker: Intermittent 95th percentile latency spikes when batch size > 6 on p4d pool
- Next action & owner & date: SE to run controlled load test w/ kernel flags and attach perf traces by 2025-02-09
- Renewal signal: watch
- Notes: Related to PR#458 in infra (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/458). Slack thread: #athena-inference (see linked_artifacts).

Blocker taxonomy (to make triage consistent):
- CUSTOMER-CONFIG: Missing IAM rules, VPC peering, internal firewall rules
- INFRA-THROTTLE: GPU or network capacity constraints; autoscale misconfig
- MODEL-QUALITY: hallucination/regression flagged by evals or QA
- PERFORMANCE-REGRESSION: token/time regressions >20% on Canary compared to baseline
- SECURITY/COMPLIANCE: KMS/HSM integration issues, audit/logging gaps

Escalation playbook (quick flow):
1) Owner identifies blocker and posts to CS signal board row with the taxonomy tag and copy to #cs-escalations.
2) If RED, ping SRE and Serving Runtime lead and schedule emergency sync within 4 hours. Attach perf traces, stack traces, and repro steps.
3) If YELLOW and impacting canary, open a tech-incident ticket and schedule a joint working session during the next 24–48 hours.
4) If CUSTOMER-CONFIG, Solutions Eng to own network/permissions checklist and confirm by EOD.

Renewal health scoring (quick heuristic for QBR prep):
- Score metrics (0–10 each): Go-live progress, Performance SLAs, Feature parity, Support volume trend, Exec engagement
- Sum and bucket: 40–50 (Healthy), 25–39 (Watch), <25 (At risk)
- Use lane + renewal score to prioritize playbook actions for QBR decks.

Meeting cadence and artifacts: 
- Weekly CS Standup (30 min): review all REDs, top 3 YELLOWs, confirm owners and blockers.
- Biweekly Technical Deep-dive (1 hr): invited SE, infra, SRE for YELLOW -> RED transitions. Bring traces and latest evals.
- QBR (quarterly): include renewal health score, milestone velocity, and list of unresolved escalations (owner + SLAs for resolution).

Notes to self / TODOs: 
- Add column for "expected token mix" for Dedicated customers to better predict batching configs (action: Liam to prototype schema).
- Consider a lightweight Zapier/GSheets integration to auto-pull last week's error rates from Observability (opens a ticket: JIRA-7812).
- Draft a short customer-facing go-live checklist (1 page) to hand to PMs and stakeholders; this doc should link to it.

Unresolved questions / discussion points: 
- Do we want to add a severity weight for renewal scoring based on ARR? (e.g., larger customers get heavier weighting). Pros/cons in comments.
- How granular should the performance thresholds be for YELLOW->RED promotions? Current heuristic is 20% deviation — needs consensus.

Appendix: quick links and examples
- Canonical go-live checklist (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/GoLive+Checklist+Draft
- Perf regression example (internal): https://internal.redwood.ai/run/trace/8721
- Customer onboarding template (sheet): shared_drives/customer-success/onboarding-template-cs-v2 (NOTE: rename to stable id)

Owner signoff (for QBR export):
- CS owner: Aisha Patel (please confirm status before 2025-02-10 meeting)
- Technical owner: Miguel Torres

End of doc.

(Informal notes sprinkled in — this is meant to be copied into a sheet per-customer for operational usage; keep short rows and link longer notes.)
